canonical_name: Paradigms of Artificial Intelligence Programming -- Norvig's Common Lisp programs (GPS, ELIZA, pattern matcher, unifier, Prolog-in-Lisp, 1991)
lineage: The canonical Common Lisp exposition of classical AI machinery: Newell & Simon's General Problem Solver (means-ends analysis), Weizenbaum's ELIZA (pattern-directed rewriting), STUDENT, a unifier and a Prolog interpreter/compiler, search tools, Othello. Real problem-solving programs from the symbolic-AI culture, kept runnable by Norvig's repository under SBCL.
version: github.com/norvig/paip-lisp main as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)
entry_points: lisp/auxfns.lisp then lisp/gps.lisp (GPS), lisp/eliza.lisp, lisp/patmatch.lisp, lisp/unify.lisp, lisp/prolog.lisp

example.input: the 'drive son to school' GPS problem (school-ops)
example.output: the plan: look up number, telephone shop, tell shop problem, give shop money, shop installs battery, drive son to school (the book's ORACLE)

upstream_docs: Norvig, Paradigms of Artificial Intelligence Programming, Morgan Kaufmann 1991
Newell & Simon, GPS, a program that simulates human thought, 1961

human_capability_summary.built_to: solve problems by reducing goal/state differences with operators (GPS), converse by pattern rewriting (ELIZA), and answer queries by unification and backtracking (Prolog)
human_capability_summary.pressure: the symbolic-AI programme's demand for general methods; the book's demand that they be small and readable
human_capability_summary.success_means: GPS finds the operator sequence the book prints; ELIZA responds; the Prolog interpreter answers member/append queries

known_human_problem_solved: classical AI problem solving in Lisp
human_environmental_pressure: combinatorial search, goal interaction (the 'prerequisite clobbers sibling goal' problem GPS exposes)
human_failure_condition: GPS loops or 'running around the block' (the book's own catalogue of GPS failures)
behavioral_entry_point: feed GPS the book's pathological goal orderings (leaping before you look; recursive subgoals) and watch it fail as documented

lineage_relations.note: Lisp family: programs vs language machine

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run paip-lisp-norvig-1991
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: solve problems by reducing goal/state differences with operators (GPS), converse by pattern rewriting (ELIZA), and answer queries by unification and backtracking (Prolog)
